Net equity = property value − selling costs − loan balance. Total return = after-tax cash flow to date + net equity − tax on the sale + tax saved by held losses − cash invested. Tax on the sale is charged on the gain: sale price − selling costs − (purchase price + closing costs + renovation − depreciation taken). The part of the gain that comes from depreciation is taxed at your bracket, capped at 25%; the rest at your long-term gains rate. State tax and the 3.8% net investment income tax are not included, and a loss on sale is shown as no tax. Same cash invested elsewhere = what your cash invested would have earned at 4% a year, compounded yearly, if you had put all of it in on day one. Income tax = (net operating income − mortgage interest − depreciation) × your tax bracket. A loss saves no tax that year. It is held, offsets later rental profit first, and whatever is left is used when you sell. Depreciation starts once the property is ready to rent, so year 1 counts only the months after renovation. While the property is being renovated there is no rent, but property tax, insurance and HOA dues still count.
